recentItems.title: Kazakh President Tokayev meets South Korean President Lee for summit in Seoul
recentItems.description:
(15 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Seoul, South Korea -  15 September 2026

1. Wide of Kazakhstan President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and South Korean President Lee Jae Myung arriving at the honor guard ceremony
2. Various of Tokayev and Lee during the honor guard ceremony
3. Mid of Tokayev and Lee shaking hands
4. Various of Tokayev and Lee during the bilateral summit
STORYLINE:
Kazakhstan President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with the South Korean President Lee Jae Myung on Tuesday afternoon for a bilateral summit ahead of the inaugural Korea-Central Asia Summit.

Tokayev was welcomed with an honor guard ceremony, which was followed by talks in South Korea's presidential office.

Tokayev will be one of the five Central Asian leaders participating in the Korea-Central Asia Summit. 

South Korea is hosting the leaders of five Central Asian nations - Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan - during the summit.

AP video by Yong-ho Kim

recentItems.title: Pamela Anderson, Martha Stewart share love for Carolina Herrera at New York show
recentItems.description:
(15 Sep 2026) 
ASSOCIATED PRESS
New York - 14 September 2026
1. Various Pamela Anderson
2. SOUNDBITE (English) Pamela Anderson, actor: 
"I just, I love the clothes. I've had a lot of fun wearing her and I was just at the Venice Film Festival and wore a couple of looks from her. But I just love the color, I love the fun. This kind of reminds me a little bit about a New York lady. It's my socialite. My attempt at that."
3. SOUNDBITE (English) Fran Lebowitz, writer: 
"I'm not the person to ask, really. To me, the clothes are great, they were always great. I'm sure they're different, but you may notice I don't actually wear those kind of clothes. But luckily, many people do."
(Reporter: "What do you love about the brand?")
"What I love actually is Carolina, personally."
(Reporter: "What's your relationship like with Carolina?")
"I've known her I was trying to think, I mean I think I've known her since... I don't know like maybe 1980 or something like that? So obviously I like her if I still know her."
(Reporter: "What's the friendship been like over all of these years, supporting your friend who has this brand?")
"You know, I have many friends I love, and that is not because they're any brands, because I'm old."
4. Various Martha Stewart
5. SOUNDBITE (English) Martha Stewart, writer: 
"Well, I think her longevity speaks for her popularity, of course, and she's a personal friend. We share a beautiful town in Maine, Seal Harbor, and, well, she's in Northeast (Hatbor), but that's the same thing. And I just love her, the beauty of her fashion. And I love Wes Gordon too, I've known him for quite a long time and he's done an amazing shepherding of her brand."
6. Various Carolina Herrera
7. Medium Ed Westwick
8. Various of catwalk show
9. Various final pass
10. Wide shot Wes Gordon on catwalk
11. SOUNDBITE (English) Wes Gordon, designer:
"So I opened with black, white, and yellow, which are very signature to Herrera. And, in fact, the first Herrera fragrance was black and white polka dots with a yellow border. And then from there we went into beautiful pinks and pistachios and blacks and reds and blues. Color has been so important to me since I started eight years ago and I've worked so hard to make Herrera synonymous with color. The colors are never sad, they're vibrant, they're electric, they are alive, just like the colors of Andy Warhol. So it was really a treat this season to collaborate with the Warhol Foundation and be able to use her iconic portrait on handbags as well as a dress."
++ENDS ON SOUNDBITE++
STORYLINE:
The Carolina Herrera show in New York was a star-studded affair, with Pamela Anderson, Martha Stewart and more in attendance. 

The celebrities shared their love for the brand, but also for the label's founder.

"Well, I think her longevity speaks for her popularity, of course, and she's a personal friend," said Stewart, who was sitting front row. 

"We share a beautiful town in Maine, Seal Harbor, and, well, she's in Northeast (Harbor), but that's same thing. And I just love her, the beauty of her, of her fashion,

Designer Wes Gordon chose to kick off the runaway show with signature Herrera colours. 

"So I opened with black, white, and yellow, which are very signature to Herrera. And in fact, the first Herrera fragrance was black and white polka dots with a yellow border," he explained. 

As well as the primary colors, he used prints of the New Yorker magazine, and collaborated with the Warhol Foundation to use some of the late artist's Iconic prints on handbags.  

The collection contained many formal gowns, as well as smart but more casual looks.

recentItems.title: I AmA Camera interview
recentItems.description:
(22 Aug 2013) 

STORYLINE:
1. SOUNDBITE (English) Francesca Ross & Ian Watt, I Am A Camera - on whether they had musical upbringings:
Reporter "Did you have musical childhoods?"
Ross: "Yeah, I've always been singing. Like I started doing gigs when I was about 10, on my own, and then I've been in bands since I was about 12, get through my teenage years and do all the girl bands that I'll kind of just skim over. But I've always been in bands, always done music, always known that that's what I've wanted to do. No one is in music in my family, but they're all massive music lovers, so just growing up around all different kinds of music and yeah, then always being in bands, working with different people. That's what I did."
Wattalways loved music, but I wanted to be a painter when I was a kid. I was always a little kid who was running around with art pads and drawing and painting the family and annoying t: "Not at all. I he hell out of them. But I've always had a love of music, it's just as I got older I kind of realized that it was kind of shifting as I got older."
2. SOUNDBITE (English) Ian Watt, I Am A Camera - on when he realized he was musical:
"I kind of figured out I could do it. I've kind of always had it in the back of my head. I've always loved it, but I think it was just kind of... I just started kind of painting and then I thought 'but I do love music.' I've always kind of played guitar and played a bit of keyboards and had those sort of things around the house, so... And then gradually I was sort of like 'oh, that's alright, that's a tune.'"
3. SOUNDBITE (English) Francesca Ross & Ian Watt, I Am A Camera - on how important visuals are to the band:
Watt: "I think so. I think for me it comes from being a kid and painting and doing all that, it feels to me like it's the same thing. It doesn't feel any different to (music.) So when I do things when I write things, visually I'll see it in there as well, so I will have a picture of who that person is and I kind of almost kind of do some strange type of photo with it and I'll always have scraps of paper and adding things. So if I have a page of lyrics I will have things with it where I know the references are always there. So it's like that for me."
Ross: "I think everything with music and art and fashion, they all run parallel together and they all influence each other and they're all massive things for us. The visual side of things, bands that I've always liked, my favorite bands are all very visual. I think it's good for people who like us not just to have things to listen to, you know, things to connect it to, have things to look at visually."

recentItems.title: Ukraine backs ongoing efforts to reach an ‘energy ceasefire,’ foreign minister says
recentItems.description:
(15 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTIONS SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Kyiv, Ukraine - 15 September 2026
1. Wide of Monaco's Foreign Minister Isabelle Berro-Amadeï and Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha at a press briefing
2. SOUNDBITE(Ukrainian) Andrii Sybiha, Ukrainian Foreign Minister: " We welcome the efforts of the United States to achieve a so-called energy ceasefire. Ukraine is ready for such a ceasefire. Our partners know our position. There are also several proposals from our closest partners and other international partners on how to move forward on this track and jointly achieve an energy ceasefire. Once again, we welcome these efforts and hope they will lead to the desired result."
3. Close of Ukrainian flag
4. Mid of Isabelle Berro-Amadeï and Andrii Sybiha shaking hands and leaving
STORYLINE:
Ukrainian Foreign Minister, Andrii Sybiha, said Ukraine is supporting efforts to achieve a so-called energy ceasefire.

Speaking during during a press briefing in Kyiv, with Monaco's Foreign Minister Isabelle Berro-Amadeï on Tuesday, Sybiha welcomed the efforts of the United States to achieve the so-called energy ceasefire. 

"Ukraine is ready for such a ceasefire. Our partners know our position," Sybiha said.

The statement comes a day after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that Ukraine was ready to halt its strikes on Russian territory if allies could secure a genuine Russian commitment not to hit Ukraine’s critical infrastructure.

His comments came after U.S. President Donald Trump claimed in a social media post that Russia and Ukraine had agreed “not to hit” each other’s energy infrastructure, though Trump did not offer further details on the purported agreement.

Russia did not immediately comment on Trump's claim. Previous efforts to broker even a partial ceasefire have repeatedly fallen apart within hours, with both sides accusing each other of violations.

Trump did not offer further details about the agreement but it comes a day after the U.S. president called on Zelenskyy to stop targeting Russian oil refineries and other infrastructure used to produce and distribute diesel, claiming the attacks are causing a global shortage. Diesel prices have surged in the U.S., and high fuel costs associated with the Iran war have become a major issue for Trump’s party in upcoming congressional elections.

recentItems.title: Southern Lebanon women show their skill and resilience at a Tyre craft fair
recentItems.description:
(15 Sep 2026) 
LEBANON UNIFL WOMEN DISPLACED

SOURCE: ASSOCIATED PRESS

RESTRICTION SUMMARY: 

LENGTH: 3:51

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Tyre, Lebanon -  12 September 2026
1. Various of Inas Kteish, a crochet crafter from Tyre city, preparing her crochet items, such as hats and wallets, to take to the fair on Tyre corniche
2. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Inas Kteish, crochet crafter participating in the fair: 
“The fairs are very important here, especially in the city of Tyre, because they help support women and enable them to provide for themselves and their families, especially at this time, when there aren’t many job opportunities, the (financial) situation is tight and resources are limited. So, we create our work by hand. We work from our homes, produce our goods, sell them, and earn an income from them.”

3. Various of Kteish collecting her crochet items, leaving her craft workshop and heading toward the fair
4. Wide of handcrafts fair in Tyre with visitors and UNIFIL soldiers passing by display tables
5. Wide of Kteish showing visitors and shoppers her items 
6. Various of Chinese UNIFIL soldier checking the displayed items at Kteish's table 
7. Wide of fair showing several display partitions, and Tyre corniche in the background
8. Various of different sections and vendors at the fair 
9. Close on handmade lantern
10. Close of crochet items, UNIFIL soldiers in the background 

11. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Rania Shaker, crafter participating in the Tyre fair: 
“Honestly, during the war (between Israel and Hezbollah militants), we had a lot of time to work. In our own way, we were resisting by showing that life has to go on. So, throughout the war, we kept making, but there was no way to market (sell our products). Now, they have given us the opportunity to market (sell) the items we make with all our heart. With handmade crafts, we create it (with love) from the bottom of our hearts.” 

12. Various of women checking out displayed accessories
13. Wide of Ibtissam Fawaz, a seller of homemade pantry items known as "Mouneh" in Arabic, sitting at her display table 
14. Close at packed homemade pantry items, including Labneh balls, thick strained yogurt, and za'atar, a seed and spice blend
15. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Ibtissam Fawaz, seller of homemade pantry items: 
“We’re encouraging people to come and buy our pantry homemade preserve so we can sort out our (financial) situation. This is how we challenge the circumstances, challenge Israel, and challenge everything we have been through.” 

16. Various of Malaysian UNIFIL soldiers buying accessories 
17. Wide of Malaysian UNIFIL soldiers checking homemade pantry items on another display table
18. Various of Chinese UNIFIL soldiers checking locally crafted perfumes
19. SOUNDBITE (English) Maj. General Diodato Abagnara, Force Commander of UNIFIL: 
“Our mission is to just to create the best condition to implement resolution 1701. Not only to protect civilians to monitor and to report, but also to support people because a strong link between different communities is the only way to create the best condition for peace.” 

20. Wide of UNIFIL Force commander Maj. General Diodato Abagnara, with the organizer of the fair Randa Abou Saleh, a member of Tyre Municipality
21. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Randa Abou Saleh, fair organizer:

22. Various of the fair with visitors passing by at sunset
STORYLINE:
Inas Kteish was busy packing her crochet items in her workshop in Tyre to head a fair along the city’s Mediterranean coast.





With the fair, she can finally sell the items that she's been poring over.

recentItems.title: Daily China MOFA Briefing Highlights
recentItems.description:
(15 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY: 

MOFA Highlights                                      
Spokesperson: Guo Jiakun
Date: 15 September 2026
Duration:  03 min 27 sec

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Beijing -  15 September 2026

Spokesperson: Guo Jiakun

1. Last Friday, the Philippine Foreign Ministry issued a statement saying that Mischief Reef and Subi Reef are low-tide elevations within the Philippines' exclusive economic zone and continental shelf, and that the Philippines has sovereign rights and jurisdiction over them. But later, it changed its position, saying that Subi Reef is a low-tide elevation within the territorial sea of Thitu Island and that the Philippines has sovereignty over it. The Philippines also said China’s construction activities on the above-mentioned islets violate the Philippines' Maritime Zones Act, the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea and the South China Sea arbitration award. What is China's comment?

The Nansha Islands (known as Spratly Islands in English), including Mischief Reef, Subi Reef and Thitu Island, are China's inherent territory. China's construction and other activities on its own territory fall within the scope of its sovereignty and are legitimate and lawful.
The extent of Philippine territory is clearly defined by a series of international treaties. The Nansha Islands have never been part of Philippine territory. In accordance with the international law principle that land territory determines maritime areas, the Philippines' claim to maritime jurisdiction over Chinese territory is illegal.
The Philippine statement first claimed that China's Subi Reef is located within its exclusive economic zone and continental shelf, and then changed its position saying that it is within the territorial waters of islands and reefs that it has illegally occupied. This only exposes how absurd and random its claim is, making it totally untenable. 
The South China Sea arbitration case was entirely a political manipulation by the Philippines to seek illegal gains. The so-called award is illegal, null and void and has no binding force. The Philippines' so-called Maritime Zones Act illegally includes China's Huangyan Island (Scarborough Shoal in English) and most of the islands and reefs of the Nansha Islands and their adjacent waters into Philippine maritime zones. This seriously infringes upon China's territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests in the South China Sea, which is illegal and null and void. China firmly opposes and will never accept it.
I would like to stress again that China will continue to take resolute measures to safeguard its territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests and firmly oppose any infringement. The Philippine side should immediately stop its provocation and infringement and stop playing up the issue.

2. A U.S. military official said yesterday that the U.S. is facing a shortfall of ammunition for its war in Iran. What is China's comment?

China is following the current situation in the Middle East and the Gulf region and hopes that the parties concerned will adhere to political and diplomatic means to resolve disputes.

3. The U.S. Space Force said yesterday that the U.S. has weapons deployed in space. What is China's response? Does China also have space weapons in orbit?

China always upholds the peaceful use of outer space, maintains outer space security, and opposes the weaponization, militarization and an arms race in outer space. We urge the U.S. to stop expanding its military preparations in outer space and take concrete actions to safeguard global strategic stability.

recentItems.title: Las pizarras de las aulas japonesas se convierten en lienzos de un arte hermoso
recentItems.description:
(15 Sep 2026) 
JAPON ARTE PIZARRON SP
Source: ASSOCIATED PRESS

Video de AP por Mayuko Ono
 
Las pizarras de las aulas japonesas se convierten en lienzos de un arte hermoso.
 
——————————————————————————————————————————
ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Saitama, Japón - 21 de julio de 2026
 
Las pizarras tradicionales se están utilizando en Japón para crear un nuevo tipo de arte, Kokuban Art Koshien, obras creadas con tiza sobre pizarras escolares.
 
En una aula de la Escuela Secundaria Femenina de Kumagaya, las alumnas intercambian ideas y revisan trabajos anteriores y libros de arte para sus creaciones.
 
La pizarra sirve de lienzo, y las tizas de colores de pintura, y estas jóvenes artistas participan en un campeonato nacional anual de arte con tiza.
 
SONIDO (japonés) Chiho Ninomiya, estudiante participante en el “Kokuban Art Koshien”: 
“Las tizas pueden ser complicadas, ya que son diferentes a los lápices y pinceles”, dijo esta estudiante. “Vamos probando y experimentando para encontrar el mejor efecto mediante frotados y difuminados.”
 
Mako Kato, quien aspira a ser profesora algún día, siente una gran afinidad por este medio. 
 
SONIDO (japonés) Mako Kato, estudiante participante en el “Kokuban Art Koshien”: 
 “Creo que la pizarra es un medio especial a través del cual puedes expresarte con pasión”, dijo.

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Tokio, Japón - 18 de mayo de 2026

Para Tomohiro Yoshida, presidente de la empresa Nichigaku organizadora del concurso, esta forma de arte  es una manera de transmitir una lección sobre la impermanencia de la vida, la fragilidad de la creación y la valentía para seguir adelante. 
 
SONIDO (japonés) Tomohiro Yoshida, presidente de Nichigaku: 
“Al igual que en la filosofía japonesa, nada dura para siempre”, afirmó.  “La obra en la que has invertido tanto tiempo y esfuerzo tendrá que ser borrada.” 
 
Pero para la estudiante Ninomiya el sentimiento es diferente.
 
SOUNDBITE (japonés) Chiho Ninomiya, estudiante participante en el "Kokuban Art Koshien" de este año: 
“Aunque no ganemos ningún premio, habrá valido la pena si fortalecemos nuestra amistad durante el proceso”.
 
ANNE MARIE GARCIA, ASSOCIATED PRESS
